headlines.title: Free signup often still blocks shipping to customers
headlines.text: 56 of 100 apps let a developer get credentials for free, but 16 of those still need an app review, marketplace listing, or partner program before you can serve many customers.
headlines.template: {free_dev} of {n} apps let a developer get credentials for free, but {free_but_gated} of those still need an app review, marketplace listing, or partner program before you can serve many customers.

headlines.title: Most apps already ship an official MCP server
headlines.text: 86 of 100 apps publish an official MCP server. 14 of those are not in the Composio catalog yet — ready coverage opportunities.
headlines.template: {mcp_off} of {n} apps publish an official MCP server. {mcp_no_comp} of those are not in the Composio catalog yet — ready coverage opportunities.

headlines.title: Easy wins you can build without a sales call
headlines.text: 64 of 100 apps look ready to integrate today (score 8–10, no partnership gate). 8 of those are still missing from Composio.
headlines.template: {easy_total} of {n} apps look ready to integrate today (score 8–10, no partnership gate). {easy_no_comp} of those are still missing from Composio.

headlines.title: Some apps need outreach no matter how good the API is
headlines.text: 12 of 100 apps require a partnership, sales contact, or partner program before you can build — 5 of those are not in Composio yet. The densest category is Finance and Fintech (4 apps).
headlines.template: {outreach_total} of {n} apps require a partnership, sales contact, or partner program before you can build — {outreach_no_comp} of those are not in Composio yet. The densest category is {top_outreach_cat} ({top_outreach_n} apps).

headlines.title: The most common reason an app is hard to integrate
headlines.text: The most common blocker is getting developer credentials (paid plans, admin approval, or partner signup) (48 of 100 apps, 48%).

headlines.title: REST and OAuth 2.0 are the default pattern
headlines.text: 91 of 100 apps expose a REST API and 74 support OAuth 2.0 (37 of those still document an extra gate before production). 64 apps offer two or more ways to authenticate.
